3.3 The Association shall not be liable to pay any amount in excess of the consolidated fee except for:
   a) Replacement parts costing more than Rs. 2,000/- per instance, which shall be billed at actuals plus 15% handling charges, subject to prior written approval of the Association;
   b) Any additional work specifically requested by the Association in writing, which shall be quoted by the Contractor and approved before commencement.

7.2 The party affected by a Force Majeure Event shall promptly notify the other party in writing of the occurrence of such event and shall use its reasonable endeavours to mitigate the effects of such event and to resume performance of its obligations as soon as practicable.

**AGENDA ITEM 2: REVIEW OF WATER SUPPLY INCIDENT OF 17–18 MARCH 2025**

The Committee discussed in detail the disruption of water supply that occurred on the night of 17 March and continued into the morning of 18 March 2025. The following facts were noted from the maintenance log and the report submitted by the plumber, Mr. D. Kulkarni:

- At approximately 23:40 on 17 March, the duty watchman reported a drop in pressure in the overhead tank supply lines.
- The borewell pump (Pump 2) was found to have tripped. On inspection, the motor winding was found burnt.
- Pump 2 was out of service from 00:15 to 14:30 on 18 March. During this period, water was supplied from the municipal connection only, which is inadequate for the full colony.
- Residents of Towers A, B, and C on the upper floors (7th floor and above) reported no water from 06:00 to 12:00 on 18 March.
- A temporary replacement pump was arranged from the local supplier at 09:00 on 18 March, and repairs to the original pump were completed by 14:30. Full normal supply resumed by 16:00 on 18 March.

The Committee noted that the incident was caused by a combination of factors:
1. The age of Pump 2 (installed in 2016, beyond its recommended service life of 8 years).
2. Voltage fluctuation on the evening of 17 March, as recorded in the electrical log.
3. The absence of a standby pump, as the earlier standby pump (Pump 3) had been removed in January 2025 for repairs and had not been reinstalled.

The minutes of the previous meeting held on 25 February 2025 were circulated to all members via email on 28 February 2025. No corrections were proposed.

**Vote:** Unanimous (8 in favour, 0 against, 0 abstentions)

---

**AGENDA ITEM 2: REVIEW OF WATER SUPPLY INCIDENT OF 17–18 MARCH 2025**

The Committee discussed in detail the disruption of water supply that occurred on the night of 17 March and continued into the morning of 18 March 2025. The following facts were noted from the maintenance log and the report submitted by the plumber, Mr. D. Kulkarni:

- At approximately 23:40 on 17 March, the duty watchman reported a drop in pressure in the overhead tank supply lines.
- The borewell pump (Pump 2) was found to have tripped. On inspection, the motor winding was found burnt.
- Pump 2 was out of service from 00:15 to 14:30 on 18 March. During this period, water was supplied from the municipal connection only, which is inadequate for the full colony.
- Residents of Towers A, B, and C on the upper floors (7th floor and above) reported no water from 06:00 to 12:00 on 18 March.
- A temporary replacement pump was arranged from the local supplier at 09:00 on 18 March, and repairs to the original pump were completed by 14:30. Full normal supply resumed by 16:00 on 18 March.

The Committee noted that the incident was caused by a combination of factors:
1. The age of Pump 2 (installed in 2016, beyond its recommended service life of 8 years).
2. Voltage fluctuation on the evening of 17 March, as recorded in the electrical log.
3. The absence of a standby pump, as the earlier standby pump (Pump 3) had been removed in January 2025 for repairs and had not been reinstalled.

**Discussion:** Mr. S. Deshmukh pointed out that the delay in reinstalling Pump 3 was due to a pending quotation from the vendor, which had been delayed because of the Holi holidays. He confirmed that the quotation has now been received and the reinstatement work is scheduled for the first week of April 2025.

The meeting minutes record that Amitabh Rao's meeting_date is 2025-03-25. Record status: current.

**RESOLUTION 2025-03-02:** The Committee approves the payment of ₹18,500 towards the repair of Pump 2, as per the invoice from M/s. Jayant Electricals, dated 19 March 2025. The amount shall be debited from the Maintenance Fund under the head "Repairs – Water Supply."

**Moved by:** Mr. R. Menon
**Seconded by:** Ms. L. Fernandes
**Vote:** Unanimous (8 in favour, 0 against, 0 abstentions)

**RESOLUTION 2025-03-03:** The Committee directs the Secretary, Mr. Amitabh Rao, to issue a notice to the vendor M/s. Jayant Electricals to complete the reinstatement of Pump 3 by 7 April 2025. In the event of delay, the vendor shall be liable for a penalty of ₹500 per day, as per the terms of the service agreement.

**Moved by:** Mr. H. Singh
**Seconded by:** Mr. A. Nair
**Vote:** Unanimous (8 in favour, 0 against, 0 abstentions)

---

**AGENDA ITEM 3: ANNUAL BUDGET FOR FY 2025–26**

The Treasurer, Mr. S. Deshmukh, presented the draft annual budget for the financial year 2025–26 (April 2025 to March 2026). Key figures are summarised below:

| Insurance (colony assets) | 1,20,000 |
| Administrative expenses | 1,80,000 |

| **Total** | **49,00,000** |

The budget assumes an increase of 8% in salaries and 6% in electricity charges over the current year. The maintenance fee is proposed to remain unchanged at ₹3.50 per sq. ft. per month for apartments and ₹2.00 per sq. ft. per month for commercial units.
